outcome: No result advancing, restricting, or resolving Podewski's conjecture in characteristic zero was found since 26 January 2024; the conjecture remains exactly as stated in the pre-2024 literature.
summary: Podewski's conjecture — every infinite minimal field (every definable subset finite or co-finite) is algebraically closed — was proved in positive characteristic by Wagner, and the characteristic-zero case has been open since at least the 2012/2013 paper 'Around Podewski's conjecture' by Krupiński, Tanović and Wagner (arXiv:1201.5709, Fundamenta Mathematicae 222 (2013)), which reduces the conjecture to a question about definable well-partial-orders and proves the 'almost linear' special case. I searched broadly for any post-January-2024 activity: general queries on Podewski's conjecture and minimal fields, targeted arXiv math.LO listing and site searches for 2024-2026, searches for the specific researchers active in this area (Wagner, Halevi, Hasson, Tanović, Krupiński) and their recent output, and a check of the closest-looking hits that turned up. None addressed the characteristic-zero case of Podewski's conjecture. Several near-misses were checked and ruled out as distinct problems under §3.1's scope rule: (1) Szachniewicz–Ye, 'Hyperbolicity and model-complete fields' (arXiv:2403.15300, published IMRN 2025) cites the already-known (pre-2024) Koenigsmann result on 'large fields' only in passing and does not engage with the characteristic-zero conjecture; (2) the classification of VC-minimal/dp-small fields as algebraically or real closed (Guingona's 2014 conjecture, proved by Guingona–Laskowski, published EMS/JEMS ~2022) concerns a different technical notion ('VC-minimal'/'dp-small', a combinatorial dividing-line condition) rather than 'minimal' in Podewski's strict model-theoretic sense (every definable subset finite or cofinite), and in any case predates the window; (3) 'On regular groups and fields' (Halevi–Hasson–Peterzil-adjacent work, arXiv:1211.3852, 2012) proving generically stable minimal/quasi-minimal fields are algebraically closed is also pre-2024 background, already known to the triage pass; (4) Acosta López–Hasson, 'On groups and fields definable in 1-h-minimal fields' (arXiv:2303.01127, published J. Inst. Math. Jussieu 2025) concerns Hensel-minimality ('1-h-minimal'), an unrelated valued-field notion, not Podewski-minimality; (5) a December 2025 survey by Jahnke and coauthors on tame valued fields' open questions does not mention Podewski's conjecture at all; (6) an ICM 2026 invited lecture 'Henselianity and NIP fields' (likely Jahnke) was found only behind a paywall (SIAM/epubs, 403 Forbidden) and could not be opened — noted as a source I could not reach. No AI system was found anywhere near this problem. I agree with the triage verdict of 'none' and its underlying reasoning.
competing_reading: It is conceivable the paywalled ICM 2026 'Henselianity and NIP fields' survey or lecture contains a remark updating the status of Podewski's conjecture (e.g., citing a very recent unpublished result or restating it as still fully open), since ICM surveys of this kind often summarize the state of adjacent open problems. I could not access it to check. This is unlikely to change the classification given how much closer literature and researcher-specific searching turned up nothing, but it is the one unresolved gap.
what_would_settle_it: Access to the ICM 2026 'Henselianity and NIP fields' article (SIAM ebooks / epubs.siam.org, DOI 10.1137/25M1805412) to confirm it does not report new progress on Podewski's conjecture in characteristic zero.
